## Key terms

{{< glossary angle degree right-triangle hypotenuse sine cosine tangent unit-circle radian unit-vector velocity quadrant >}}

## 7.1 Which way is the drone facing? Angles

- The **angle** of a direction is the turn from the +x axis, in
  **degrees** (°).
- 0° points right (+x), 90° up (+y), 180° left (−x), 270° down (−y).
- A positive angle turns **anticlockwise**; a negative angle turns
  clockwise. −45° is the same direction as 315°.
- A full turn is 360°. Two angles that differ by 360° give the same
  direction: 370° = 10°.
- Unity turns a 2D object anticlockwise for a positive angle too.

![Angles in game maths.](images/angle-dial.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
On a map, 0° is north and angles turn clockwise. In game maths, 0° is +x
and angles turn anticlockwise.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Draw five headings"}
On squared paper, draw the axes and arrows for 0°, 90°, 135°, 225° and −45°
(use the diagonals of the squares for 45°). Write the second name of each
angle, for example 270° = −90°.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Headings"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="down (−y)|200°"}
A drone has the heading 90°. Which way does it fly?
:   up (+y)

A drone has the heading 180°. Which way does it fly?
:   left (−x)

Which angle is the same direction as −90°?
:   270°

A turret faces 350° and turns 20° anticlockwise. Which angle does it face?
:   10°

On a map, east is 90°. Which angle is east in game maths?
:   0°
:::
:::

## 7.2 How high is the ramp? Sine, cosine and tangent

- A **right triangle** has one angle of 90°.
- For the angle θ: the **hypotenuse** is the longest side, the
  **opposite** side is across from θ, the **adjacent** side is next to θ.
- sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse; cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse;
  tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.
- So: opposite = hypotenuse × sin θ, adjacent = hypotenuse × cos θ.
- tan θ is the **slope**: how far up for 1 forward.

| θ | 0° | 30° | 45° | 60° | 90° |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sin θ | 0 | 0.5 | 0.71 | 0.87 | 1 |
| cos θ | 1 | 0.87 | 0.71 | 0.5 | 0 |
| tan θ | 0 | 0.58 | 1 | 1.73 | — |

- Ramp 10 m at 30°: height 10 × 0.5 = **5 m**, forward 10 × 0.87 =
  **8.7 m**.
- Hill 3 m up over 4 m forward (slope side 5 m): sin = 0.6, cos = 0.8,
  tan = 0.75.

![The ramp as a right triangle.](images/right-triangle.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Opposite and adjacent depend on the angle you look from.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The calculator of your phone"}
Open the calculator in scientific mode (DEG, not RAD). Compute sin 30°,
cos 30° and tan 45°, and compare with the table. Then compute the height of
a 10 m ramp at 20°: 10 × sin 20°.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · The right triangle"}
Use the table above. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="opposite ÷ adjacent|20 m"}
sin θ is …
:   opposite ÷ hypotenuse

A ramp is 10 m long and rises at 30°. How high is it?
:   5 m

A ramp is 10 m long and rises at 30°. How far forward does it reach?
:   8.7 m

A hill rises 3 m over 4 m forward. What is tan θ, the slope?
:   0.75

Which side of a right triangle is the longest?
:   the hypotenuse
:::
:::

## 7.3 Every angle at once: the unit circle

- The **unit circle** has the radius 1 and the centre (0, 0).
- The point at the angle θ is **(cos θ, sin θ)**: cos is x, sin is y.
- 0°: (1, 0). 90°: (0, 1). 180°: (−1, 0). 270°: (0, −1).
- For larger angles, the same numbers come back with signs: 30° (0.87, 0.5),
  150° (−0.87, 0.5), 210° (−0.87, −0.5), 330° (0.87, −0.5).
- cos² θ + sin² θ = 1: (cos θ, sin θ) is always a **unit vector**.
- At 90° and 270°, cos θ = 0, so tan θ does not exist.

![The unit circle.](images/unit-circle.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The point is (cos θ, sin θ), not (sin θ, cos θ). At 90° it is (0, 1).
:::

{{< sim file="sims/unit-circle-lab.html" poster="sims/unit-circle-lab.png" title="Unit Circle Lab: cos, sin and tan for every angle" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Four points in Unit Circle Lab"}
In **Unit Circle Lab**, put the point at 30°, 150°, 210° and 330°. Write
cos θ and sin θ each time. What changes from row to row, and what stays the
same?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · On the circle"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(1, 0)|(0.87, −0.5)"}
The point on the unit circle at 90°.
:   (0, 1)

The point on the unit circle at 180°.
:   (−1, 0)

The point at 30° is (0.87, 0.5). The point at 150°?
:   (−0.87, 0.5)

At 210°, which signs do cos θ and sin θ have?
:   both negative

Why is (0.6, 0.8) on the unit circle?
:   0.36 + 0.64 = 1
:::
:::

## 7.4 From an angle to a movement

- The direction at the angle θ is the unit vector **(cos θ, sin θ)**.
- Velocity = speed × direction (lecture 3):
  **v = s (cos θ, sin θ) = (s cos θ, s sin θ)**.
- Drone at 30°, speed 10: 10 × (0.87, 0.5) = **(8.7, 5)**. After 2 s:
  (17.4, 10).
- Ball at 135°, speed 4: 4 × (−0.71, 0.71) ≈ **(−2.8, 2.8)**: left and up.

![The drone flies at 30° with the speed 10.](images/angle-velocity.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not multiply the speed by the angle (10 × 30 = 300 is wrong). Multiply
the speed by cos θ and by sin θ.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Velocity from the unit circle"}
A boat sails at 60° with the speed 6. In **Unit Circle Lab**, read cos 60°
and sin 60°. Multiply both by 6. Check: is the length of your vector about
6?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Velocity"}
Use the table of section 7.2. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(5, 8.7)|300"}
A drone flies at 30° with the speed 10. Its velocity?
:   (8.7, 5)

A car drives at 0° with the speed 12. Its velocity?
:   (12, 0)

A drone flies at 45° with the speed 10. Its velocity?
:   (7.1, 7.1)

A drone flies at 90° with the speed 3. Its velocity?
:   (0, 3)

A ball moves at 135°. Which way does it go?
:   left and up
:::
:::

## 7.5 What game code uses: radians

- Game code measures angles in **radians**, not degrees.
- One radian: the arc of the unit circle is 1 long. 1 rad ≈ 57°.
- 180° = π ≈ **3.14** rad; 90° ≈ **1.57** rad; 360° = 2π ≈ **6.28** rad.
- radians = degrees × π ÷ 180. In Unity: `Mathf.Deg2Rad` (≈ 0.01745).
- `Mathf.Sin(30)` reads 30 radians and gives −0.99.
  `Mathf.Sin(30 * Mathf.Deg2Rad)` gives 0.5.

```csharp
float angle = 30 * Mathf.Deg2Rad;                    // 0.52 rad
Vector2 dir = new Vector2(Mathf.Cos(angle), Mathf.Sin(angle));
Vector2 velocity = 10 * dir;                         // (8.7, 5)
```

![Degrees and radians.](images/radians.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A calculator in RAD mode gives sin 30 = −0.99. Use DEG for degrees.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · DEG and RAD"}
On your calculator, compute sin 90 in DEG mode, then in RAD mode. Then
compute sin 1.57 in RAD mode. Why is the last one 1?
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Radians"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="90|0.5 rad"}
180° in radians.
:   π ≈ 3.14

90° in radians.
:   about 1.57

About how many degrees is 1 radian?
:   57°

Which unit do `Mathf.Sin` and `Mathf.Cos` use?
:   radians

What does `30 * Mathf.Deg2Rad` give?
:   about 0.52
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Drone Drop {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Drone Drop** is a delivery game. The depot is at (0, 0). The drone flies at
the speed 10 for exactly 1 second, then drops the parcel. The player chooses
only the heading. Ana lives at (8.7, 5), Ben at (0, 10) and Cara at
(−7.1, 7.1). Each house is 10 units from the depot.

{{< sim file="sims/drone-drop.html" poster="sims/drone-drop.png" title="Drone Drop: choose the heading to each house" kind="game" height="780" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · Which heading?"}
Drone Drop: depot (0, 0), speed 10, 1 second. Ana (8.7, 5), Ben (0, 10),
Cara (−7.1, 7.1). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="60°|180°"}
Which heading reaches Ana?
:   30°

Which heading reaches Ben?
:   90°

Which heading reaches Cara?
:   135°

What is the velocity with the heading 30°?
:   (8.7, 5)
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · New customers (harder)"}
Drone Drop: depot (0, 0), speed 10, 1 second. cos 30° = 0.87,
sin 30° = 0.5. Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(5, −8.7)|(−5, −8.7)"}
The drone flies at 210°. Where does the parcel fall?
:   (−8.7, −5)

The drone flies at 330°. Where does the parcel fall?
:   (8.7, −5)

A customer lives at (0, −10). Which heading?
:   270°

The drone flies at 90° for only 0.5 seconds. Where does the parcel fall?
:   (0, 5)

In Unity, which line makes the heading 30° ready for `Mathf.Cos`?
:   30 * Mathf.Deg2Rad
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- An angle is the turn from +x, in degrees; positive angles turn anticlockwise.
- sin = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, cos = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, tan = opposite ÷ adjacent.
- The point at θ on the unit circle is (cos θ, sin θ): a unit vector.
- Velocity at the angle θ with the speed s: s (cos θ, sin θ).
- Game code uses radians: 180° = π ≈ 3.14 rad; convert with `Mathf.Deg2Rad`.
